concerns.text: T001 bundles seven distinct deliverables (download+validation, checksum, power analysis, MW filter, scaffold count, scaffold split) into one task. Each is individually verifiable and should be a separate task; as written it is too coarse for deterministic per-task execution and will need atomization.

T004 requires 'three model configurations × two learners' (Ridge AND RF) in model_performance.json 'matching model_metrics.schema.yaml', but the schema has only traditional/topological/combined keys with no model_type dimension. An implementer cannot deterministically satisfy both the task text and the contract; specify the JSON layout for the two learners or amend the schema.

T002's verification relies on 'code/tests/test_feature_matrix.py' but the task body never lists creating this test as a deliverable; the test file's creation is silently assumed. Name it as an explicit output of T002 (or of T009r) so the implementer knows who writes it.

T009r combines two unrelated deliverables — authoring unit tests for graph_builder/persistence_utils and executing the full pipeline under the resource monitor. Split into a test-authoring task and a resource-measurement task; each has a different verification ('pytest passes' vs 'resource_usage.json contains measured values').

T012r bundles a full re-run, test confirmation, and writing the paper-stage handoff section. The handoff-writing sub-deliverable (content requirements: primary claim, corrected p-value, MI context, limitations) is separable and should be its own task for verifiability.
